title: Mouse Gross Necropsy with Histology
author: Stephen M. Griffey
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.yusfwwe

steps.title: Administrative Setup
steps.instruction: Assign a CPL accession number to each animal and match it to the animal's ID (e.g., ear notch or toe snip).

substeps.instruction: Record the CPL accession number onto each sample container using a permanent pen (Sharpie).
Document any additional diagnostic requests beyond the standard necropsy.

steps.title: Animal Inspection
steps.instruction: Observe animals in the cage for visible abnormalities and record observations on the profile form.

substeps.instruction: Check for tremors, head tilt, muscular weakness, tumors, wounds, alopecia, dermatitis, eye lesions, and abscesses.
Examine external orifices for diarrhea, excessive salivation, or other signs of altered health.

steps.title: Euthanasia
steps.instruction: Euthanize each animal following the Rodent Euthanasia procedure.

substeps.instruction: Clean the CO2 chamber and lid by spraying with a 1:10 bleach solution, saturating well, and wiping with a dry paper towel.

steps.title: Animal Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the animal for necropsy and record physical data.

substeps.instruction: Weigh the whole animal on a tared scale and record weight on the profile form.
Clean the scale with a paper towel and 1:10 Lysol solution after weighing all animals.
Place the animal in dorsal recumbancy on the necropsy table and perform a thorough physical examination, recording observations on the profile form.

steps.title: Initial Incision and Skin Collection
steps.instruction: Expose the internal organs and collect skin samples.

substeps.instruction: Wet the ventrum thoroughly using a squeeze bottle with 95% ethanol.
Incise the skin along the ventral midline on both sides using forceps and/or scissors to reflect the skin/mammary glands back from the abdomen and thorax to the mandible cranially.
Place the skin/mammary glands into a 10% formalin container.

steps.title: Organ Inspection
steps.instruction: Inspect all organs for lesions or gross abnormalities, taking digital pictures of any noted lesions and recording observations on the profile form.

steps.title: Tissue Collection
steps.instruction: Collect tissues and place them in containers with a 10:1 ratio of formalin to tissue.

substeps.instruction: Gently remove all abdominal tissues (liver, kidneys, spleen, gastrointestinal tract, pancreas, urinary bladder, and reproductive tract) and place in 10% formalin; notch the right kidney.

Notch the trachea with Iris scissors. Insert a blunt aluminum hub needle attached to a syringe containing 10% formalin and gently perfuse both right and left lungs to approximately inspiratory volume. Remove the pluck (lungs, heart, and thymus) and place in formalin.
Decapitate the animal using Metzenbaum scissors. Use Iris scissors to cut open the skull cap, exposing the brain without removing it from the skull. Place the head in formalin.
Place the remaining carcass into formalin.

steps.title: Trimming Preparation
steps.instruction: Allow tissues to fix in labeled formalin containers for a minimum of 24 hours before trimming.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the following materials: 1 container of formalin-soaked sponges, clean plastic cutting board, forceps, new one-sided razor blade, small scissors, 1000 μl beaker with a strainer, plastic sample cassettes, and a permanent black marking pen.

steps.title: Cassette Labeling
steps.instruction: Label each cassette using a number 2-3 hardness pencil with the year and CPL accession number (e.g., 09-1365).

substeps.instruction: If multiple cassettes are needed per sample, use suffixes (e.g., 09-1365-A, 09-1365-B).
If sub-accessions are required, use further numbering (e.g., 09-1365-A1, 09-1365-A2).

steps.title: Tissue Trimming
steps.instruction: Trim tissues to a thickness of 2-3 mm using a razor blade or scalpel and distribute into cassettes.

substeps.instruction: Pour formalin from the sample container into a beaker with a strainer and place the sample on the cutting board.
Cassette 1: Liver (two lobes adjacent to gall bladder), Spleen (cross section), Pancreas, and Kidneys (right kidney cross section at hilus, left kidney longitudinally in half).
Cassette 2: Heart (trimmed below auricles), Lungs (cross section at level of bronchus), and mediastinal tissue (esophagus, trachea, and thymus).
Cassette 3: Mesenteric lymph node, stomach and duodenum (trimmed together), colon, and a section of the ileocecal colic junction containing the cecum.
Cassette 4: 5 cross sections of brain including brain stem, cerebellum, and cerebrum.
Cassette 5: Entire reproductive tract and urinary bladder, cross sectioned.

steps.title: Post-Trimming Processing
steps.instruction: Finalize sample storage and clean the workstation.

substeps.instruction: Place cassettes into a container filled with 10% buffered formalin.
Record tissue collection information on the Necropsy Worksheet.
Dispose of used formalin in the beaker into the labeled formalin waste container while wearing eye protection.
Clean the lab and instruments according to PAT-08 or PAT-09 procedures.

steps.title: Histologic Processing and Analysis
steps.instruction: Submit cassettes to the histology laboratory for paraffin block processing.

substeps.instruction: Cut 5 μM thick sections and stain with Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E).
Examine H&E stained slides microscopically for pathologic changes.
Document results in an excel workbook (for multiple animals) and discuss findings with the PI.
